seo.homeDescription: Find upcoming Brisbane kerbside large-item collection dates. Select a week to highlight every scheduled suburb on an interactive map.

homeFaq.question: How often is kerbside collection?
homeFaq.answer: Brisbane City Council schedules one large-item collection week per financial year for each Brisbane suburb.

homeFaq.question: When should items go on the footpath?
homeFaq.answer: Items can go out on the weekend before the collection week and must be ready by 6am on the first day.

homeFaq.question: How much can I put out?
homeFaq.answer: Council limits each pile to 2 cubic metres, roughly one small box-trailer load.

guideFaq.question: Is Brisbane kerbside collection available to every property?
guideFaq.answer: Residential households in the Brisbane local government area are eligible, including houses and multi-unit dwellings. Commercial properties, caravan parks, schools and vacant land are excluded.

guideFaq.question: Can I put a mattress out for Brisbane kerbside collection?
guideFaq.answer: Yes. Brisbane City Council currently lists mattresses as accepted kerbside items.

guideFaq.question: Can televisions and computers go out for collection?
guideFaq.answer: Yes. Electronic waste such as televisions and computer monitors is currently accepted.

guideFaq.question: Can I put out paint, glass or tyres?
guideFaq.answer: No. Council directs paint, glass, mirrors and tyres to other disposal or recycling options.

guideFaq.question: Why is my suburb missing from the kerbside search?
guideFaq.answer: The map lists current and future dates in the published open dataset. A suburb may be absent after its collection has passed or before its next date is published.

guideFaq.question: Is this the official Brisbane City Council calendar?
guideFaq.answer: No. This is an independent presentation of Council open data. Use the official calendar for final confirmation.
